title: Screen & Data Level Navigation Framework
subtitle: Streamlined 3-Domain L1 Rail with Pages L2 Roll-Up, Feed Configuration, and Screen Review Protocol

components.title: Navigating Data Levels: L1, L2, and L3 System
components.body: A unified framework mapping the application data hierarchy (Domain → Container/Query → Record/Outline) to physical navigation surfaces (Rail → Context Sidebar → Document Outline & View Controls). Features the radical simplification of L1 down to 3 core content domains (Notebooks, Journal, Pages) plus Settings, removing standalone entity rails (Notes, Sessions, Efforts, Equipment, Tags, Dashboards) by rolling them into Pages L2 subsections.

components.title: Navigation & Screen Scope
components.body: Current scale of the navigation tree, data hierarchy, and evaluated surfaces.

components.title: 1. The Unified 3-Tier Data Navigation Framework
components.body: To eliminate confusion, every screen strictly adheres to three clear data levels that map consistently between desktop columns and mobile overlays.

components.title: Data Hierarchy vs. Navigation Surface
components.body: What each level represents conceptually and where it lives physically.

items.title: Where in the universe am I?
items.body: Strictly limited to 3 Primary Content Domains: Notebooks, Journal, Pages (plus Settings pinned to bottom). All individual entity types are removed from L1. Desktop: 56px fixed left icon rail. Mobile: AppRail inside the left slide-over drawer.

items.title: What collection or filter am I in?
items.body: The current scope within the domain: Notebooks (Subscribed vs Available & Feed sources), Journal (Calendar mini-month & Notebook selector), or Pages (Subsections for Notes, Sessions, Efforts, Equipment, Tags, Dashboards, Guides). Desktop: 240px context sidebar. Mobile: slide-over left drawer body.

items.title: What piece or view mode am I manipulating?
items.body: The current record's internal structure or stream layout: 'On this page' heading anchors, runnable block list, stream layout (Cards/Rows), and date window. Desktop: 240px right rail (2xl+) or ⋯ menu. Mobile: right slide-over drawer.

components.title: The Three Primary Macro Pathways to Notes & Content (The New L1)
components.body: Every note and data record in the system is reachable through one of three intuitive top-level paths, each serving a distinct mental model.

items.title: Notebooks (/notebooks)
items.body: Index of Notebooks themselves (not flat notes). Displays subscribed notebooks by default with toggle to include unsubscribed notebooks for subscription. Per-notebook sync controls. Clicking any notebook navigates to /notebook/:slug (its README/root note). Includes 'Configure Sources' button routing to /settings feed management.

items.title: Journal (/journal, /journal/:date)
items.body: Time and calendar-centric view of daily notes and workouts. L2 provides a calendar mini-month and timeline. Default shows the user's own journal entries; provides multi-select toggles in L2 to include specific subscribed notebooks on the calendar.

items.title: Pages (/pages)
items.body: Universal flat, sortable index of all records having a unique slug (or direct note link if unslugged). Absorbs all former standalone L1 entities (Notes, Sessions, Efforts, Equipment, Tags, Guides, Dashboards) into clean L2 subsections.

components.title: L1 Rail Pruning: What Was Removed & Where It Lives Now
components.body: Consolidating 11 fragmented rail icons into Pages L2 subsections eliminates cognitive clutter and visual noise.

items.title: Notes & Dashboards
items.body: Now inside Pages L2: Select 'Notes' subsection for all notebook-member and standalone markdown notes. Select 'Dashboards' subsection for analytics explorers and custom vault dashboards.

items.title: Efforts, Equipment, & Sessions
items.body: Now inside Pages L2: Select 'Efforts' subsection for movement taxonomy and PR logs. Select 'Equipment' for gear catalog. Select 'Sessions' for completed workout execution histories.

items.title: Tags & Feeds
items.body: Now inside Pages L2 & Settings: 'Tags' is an L2 subsection of Pages grouping notes by tag taxonomy. 'Feeds' is moved out of the content rail into Settings under Source & Feed Management.

components.title: The Golden Rule of Consistency
components.body: A user must never wonder 'where am I?'. If you are viewing a single Note (/note/:id), L1 indicates its Domain (Notebooks, Journal, or Pages), L2 shows its parent Container (Notebook member list, Calendar date stack, or Pages subsection), and L3 shows its internal Outline (Headings & Blocks). L2 must never disappear.

components.title: 2. Comprehensive Screen-by-Screen Navigation Audit
components.body: Evaluating all 17 primary screens against the streamlined L1 model (Notebooks, Journal, Pages + Settings), with rolled-up L2 subsections and feed configuration.

L1: Pages (Dashboards removed from L1; lives under Pages L2 subsection 'Dashboards'). L2: Pinned & Saved Dashboards list + 'New Query' lab trigger. L3: Chart type, Aggregations, Time window.

components.title: 3. The Screen Review Framework (How to Review & Give Feedback)
components.body: Use this structured 4-step framework whenever evaluating a screen or specifying a future-state version.

components.title: The 4-Step Screen Review Checklist
components.body: Four questions to ask for every screen in the application.

items.title: 1. Where am I in the data model?
items.body: Identify the Macro data level (Notebooks, Journal, Pages, Settings), Meso data level (Parent collection, Calendar date, or Pages subsection), and Micro data level (Current entity). Ensure L1 and L2 clearly communicate this location without blank spaces or unexpected route jumps.

items.title: 2. How do I move laterally or up?
items.body: Check L2 context: Can the user switch to sibling items (e.g. other notes in the notebook, other dates in the month, other pages in the library variation) without hitting the browser Back button or returning to the root list?

items.title: 3. What can I inspect or configure here?
items.body: Check L3 context: Does the screen provide immediate access to in-page section anchors (TOC), runnable block commands, and display layout options (Cards/Rows, visible fields)?

items.title: 4. Does mobile preserve the hierarchy?
items.body: Verify mobile drawers: Left drawer must provide L1 rail + L2 scope. Right drawer must provide L3 TOC + display controls. Tapping destinations must auto-dismiss; editing filter checkboxes must retain drawer open until Apply.

components.title: How to Create Future-State Versions Using This Whiteboard
components.body: Step-by-step workflow for providing feedback and creating v2, v3, etc.

items.title: Highlight & Annotate
items.body: Open this HTML file in your browser via file://. Highlight any text row in the table above or in this document. Click 'Annotate selection' and type your feedback, desired changes, or screen redesign proposals.

items.title: Export Annotations
items.body: Click the floating pill icon in the top right corner. Click the copy icon to copy all your saved comments and quotes to your clipboard.

items.title: Prompt the Next Iteration
items.body: Paste the annotations into chat. The agent will read your feedback, update the JSON specification, and run build.py to generate navigation-screen-data-levels.v(N+1).html with your future-state screens built in.

items.title: Review Version Diffs
items.body: Open the new snapshot. Use the version history links at the top (v1, v2, etc.) to toggle between versions, observing how each screen evolved according to your notes.

components.title: 4. Priority Future-State Implementations
components.body: Core architectural updates aligned with the Streamlined L1 Rail (Notebooks, Journal, Pages + Settings) and Pages L2 Subsections.

components.title: Immediate High-Leverage Upgrades
components.body: Resolving rail bloat, establishing clean content hierarchy, and empowering source management.

items.title: Notebooks Index & Source Management
items.body: Rebuild /notebooks as an index of notebooks (not raw notes). Show subscribed notebooks by default with toggle for unsubscribed. Add sync controls and a top 'Configure Sources' button routing to /settings feeds management. Clicking opens /notebook/:slug.

items.title: Journal with Notebook Selection
items.body: Elevate Journal to its own primary L1. Default calendar shows only the user's personal journal entries. L2 provides checkboxes to include subscribed notebooks on the calendar.

items.title: Prune L1: Universal Pages Roll-Up
items.body: Remove Notes, Sessions, Efforts, Equipment, Tags, and Dashboards from the L1 rail. Roll them all into Pages L2 subsections for all entities with a unique slug or direct note link.

components.title: Ready for v2 Review
components.body: The streamlined L1 rail (Notebooks, Journal, Pages + Settings) with all entity types rolled up into Pages L2 subsections is now fully specified. Build and review v2 in your browser to continue annotating screen details.
